owner.occupation: Owner of a small resaw and kiln-drying mill

world.bio: Graham Tulloch, 58. I run a one-man timber mill on six acres outside Castlemaine, central Victoria, about two hours from Melbourne. Bandsaw resaw, a solar kiln I built from a shipping-container shell, and a shed full of clamps. Runs a small mill near Castlemaine, does de-nailing and quartersawing, mostly Victorian hardwoods, some salvaged oregon and old-growth pine when it turns up. Twenty-six years in the trade, the last eleven on my own.
skills_assets: Runs a small mill near Castlemaine, does de-nailing and quartersawing
Wood-Mizer LT40 bandsaw mill plus a 24-inch resaw bandsaw, both sharpened in-house
Solar kiln, roughly 6 cubic metres per charge, takes a green board to 10-12 percent in eight to twelve weeks depending on species
Metal detector wand and a good set of nail pullers; can de-nail and read a beam for old fixings before it touches a blade
Forklift, a tipper trailer and a 2008 Isuzu truck with a tray
Six acres with a workshop, a concrete slab and a yard that holds about 40 cubic metres of stacked stock

projects.name: Kiln and resaw capacity
projects.text: The machines sit idle most weeks since the furniture maker I supplied retired in June. He took about 70 percent of everything that came out of the kiln, mainly blackwood and Victorian ash for tables and chairs. I have two stacks of ash air-drying and a half-charge of blackwood I have been holding for him. Since he retired the phone has been very quiet. I am running the kiln three days a fortnight to keep it warm. Cost of that, mostly electric fans, is not nothing.

projects.name: Shed roof and solar upgrade
projects.text: The mill shed roof has three sheets that lift in a southerly. Quote came in at 4,800 dollars. Also want to double the panels that run the kiln fans, but that is a spring job if cash allows. Cash is not allowing right now.

projects.name: Historical society timber display
projects.text: I volunteer at the Castlemaine Historical Society on Wednesdays. We are building a display of local timber species with cross-sections and dates. I cut and plane the samples. Seventeen species so far, gum, box, stringybark, blackwood. Opening is October.

notes.text: Rang the council about the fire permit for burning off the back paddock. Told me the season starts early this year, first week of November. That is three weeks to clear the grass around the shed. Need to get the slasher on the tractor.

Haven't sawn a board for a customer in nine days. Did the quartersawn blackwood stack for myself, just to stack it. Walter retired in June and I keep expecting him to ring about the next order. He never rings. His son-in-law sold the workshop. I feel a bit stupid for having all my eggs in one basket.

Italian lesson number nineteen. Maria says my pronunciation of 'gnocchi' makes her wince. Planning the trip for next September, Piedmont and then down to Cremona, I have always wanted to see where the violins come from. Still can't order a coffee without sounding like a tourist.

Checked the kiln logger. Humidity curve looks good on the ash. If I had a use for it I'd happily do another charge but the stack I have waiting is already more than I can sell in the next six months. Might have to drop the price to move it. Hate doing that.

Wednesday at the historical society. Dorothy found an old photo of the Wesley Hill sawmill from 1911, men standing on a log the width of a ute. Wish I could get timber like that now. All the big stuff I get is from demolitions, and half of it comes with fencing wire and nails.

Sharpened both blades. Doing a small quartersawn job for a bloke in Daylesford who wants rift-cut oak for a door. Two days work, 600 dollars. That is the most revenue in a fortnight. Not going to pay the electricity bill with doors.

Phone call with my sister, she thinks I should sell up and move to the coast. I said it's not that bad. She said 'Graham, you were saying that in March'. Fair. But I like it here. I have the place paid off, mostly. The kookaburras know my schedule.

Fire plan day. Checked the pump, hoses, sprinkler on the roof. The CFA volunteer came by and said the neighbour's gum is too close to the shed, needs trimming. Added to the list. Everything is on the list.

Lay awake thinking about the kiln. Spent four years getting that thing right. Seems a waste if it only ever dries two stacks a year. Maybe I should put an ad in a few forums, 'kiln drying available, custom quartersawing, de-nailing'. Walter always said word of mouth is all you need. Word of mouth only works if the mouth is still around.
The Isuzu failed the roadworthy, brake lines. 900 dollars. Paid it. That's it for the month's mill income.

messages.text:
Fiona: Are you eating properly?
Me: Yes. I made a stew.
Fiona: With actual vegetables?
Me: There were carrots.
Fiona: Graham.

Me: Thinking of you, mate. Hope the caravan is treating you right.
Walter: Ha, the caravan is treating me like a king. We're in Bright. Leaves are turning.
Me: I still have your blackwood stack. Want me to hold it?
Walter: Sell it if you can, don't hold it for me. My hands are done.

Dorothy: Can you cut me three more samples of stringybark, about 40 cm?
Me: Sure, bring the logs Wednesday.
Dorothy: They're in the back of the Kombi.
Me: Of course they are.

Pete: How's the oak going?
Me: Quartersawn, flat as a pancake. Come Friday.
Pete: Great. Any chance you could do another door for my neighbour?
Me: Happy to. Send photos of the opening.

Broker: Your public liability is due 15 October, 2,100 dollars.
Me: Can I split it?
Broker: Can do two instalments.
Me: Please.

relations.about: Furniture maker, 71, retired in June, my main customer for eleven years, now travelling in a caravan
Younger sister in Torquay, a nurse, worries about me being alone out here
Historical society secretary, keeps asking for samples, makes the best scones in the district

constraints: Won't take on jobs requiring heavy highway driving more than two hours either way
Won't mill treated pine or anything with lead paint
Needs at least a month's notice for large kiln runs
No work on fire-ban days; no weekend work except fire prep
sensitive: Revenue is down roughly 60 percent since June
Property mostly paid off but a small overdraft is being used for insurance
Didn't tell his sister how bad the cash flow is
Mild arthritis in the left hand, wearing a brace when sawing
